content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text labels the point UNDERDETERMINED while acknowledging both a footed covenant-origin analogy and the sentence's own source statement, which is the dual-sense/open treatment K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed: (1) the judge treats the verse as open because its own words state the source while the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed; (2) under the rule, a verse with two senses at once is not open and both senses stand.","why":"The judge called the point UNDERDETERMINED even though the verse's own words state the source while the challenger's analogy is also footed, treating a two-sense verse as open contrary to K-S2."}
